<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/knowledge-pgvector`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), os knowledge rebuild (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/rebuild.ts))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION (symbol, a top-level const object), CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION (literal, a string literal in CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os knowledge rebuild (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/rebuild.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), beginBuild (symbol, a method of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter), completeBuild (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService; a method of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **43** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1c41e55e23a604c9c59430f45d05b2b3ac86837` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3197f5514a895c67201a4455e548fb3fd8453df3` — the merge of head `e5bac7e3ba7bd362eb932d7f5d8eef6a9678bf83` into base `b1c41e55e23a604c9c59430f45d05b2b3ac86837`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3197f5514a895c67201a4455e548fb3fd8453df3 && git checkout 3197f5514a895c67201a4455e548fb3fd8453df3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b1c41e55e23a604c9c59430f45d05b2b3ac86837 e5bac7e3ba7bd362eb932d7f5d8eef6a9678bf83 && git checkout -B drift-repro b1c41e55e23a604c9c59430f45d05b2b3ac86837 && git merge --no-ff e5bac7e3ba7bd362eb932d7f5d8eef6a9678bf83

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1c41e55e23a604c9c59430f45d05b2b3ac86837
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b1c41e55e23a604c9c59430f45d05b2b3ac86837` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `50bac3562b1062b21d1054699579007a03ac54f8`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #37465 (body, triage, three scope notes, claim and its amend, both os-dev-reports), PR #37570 (body, 9 files), the net diff against `main` at the head, and the head's check-runs: 0 failure; every required context green (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 10/10, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset). Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) is skipped on the PR. So the six live `build-fence.live-postgres` cases, which carry the `pg_locks` reading, have the dev's local reading only (83/83 on PG 16.16) until the queue runs.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

- `KnowledgeBuildRecord.status` gains `lease-lost` and `timed-out`. **Right.** The claim amend asked for it (Q2, option A), and the package entry exports no new name (`index.ts` still re-exports only `BUILD_LEASE_MS`, `BUILD_PROGRESS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` and `buildLockKey` from `knowledge-build.ts`). `startBuildFence`, `fencedCall` and `BUILD_STALL_LIMIT_MS` stay internal. `BUILD_STALL_LIMIT_MS` is a fixed ceiling with no setting or option, so ADR-0049 has no key to apply to, as the card allowed.
- pgvector write accept-set narrows for a build that lost its lock: an `upsert` or `delete` with `ctx.reason === 'reindex'` for a build this adapter began is refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` (409) once `pg_locks` on the lock's own session no longer shows the advisory lock. **Right.** This is the card's scope note of 09:43Z. Event-sync writes (another reason) are not fenced.
- pgvector `completeBuild` refuses `LOCK_CONFLICT` unless this adapter began the build, still holds the lock, and the generation under its fingerprint is the one it began. **Right**, the scope note of 09:57Z; the live test drives two builders.
- pgvector search exhaustion: an uncoded `Error` becomes `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` (409). **Right**, the scope note of 11:19Z (N3).
- `scripts/error-status-unpinned-baseline.json` loses `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` and `LOCK_CONFLICT`. **Right.** Both sit under "Conflict Errors (409)" in `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`, and every new producer declares 409. The baseline is shrink-only and a row that becomes pinned must leave; the conformance gate is in the green Lint & Repo Gates.

Seat questions:

1. **The lease fence in `walkObjectSource`.** It is checked before each page (top of the loop, before `engine.find`) and once after the last page, before the purge. It is **not** checked again between the purge and `completeBuild`. A renewal that hangs or a lock store that does not answer reads as lost once `heldUntil` passes, which is `startedAt + BUILD_LEASE_MS` of the last renewal that succeeded. Further embedding spend stops at the next page boundary. The page in flight (at most 100 rows) still finishes; the card's "stops at the next page" allows this. Two paths still complete after the lease is gone: a lease lost during the purge, and a purge hung past the stall bound that answers later. See S1.
2. **The stall bound.** For a hung embed call (`upsert`), and for `find`, `delete` and `beginBuild`, yes. `fencedCall` rejects at the bound, the walk returns, the `reindexTails` chain is freed, `rebuildSource` records `timed-out` and releases the lease, and the next rebuild completes (the test pins this). The progress callback is guarded on `record.status !== 'running'`. A late answer from a page call writes that page only (documented, ADR-0161 gives no abort signal); the walk then stops at its next `fence.stop()`, which keeps `timed-out`. The listing, the purge and `completeBuild` are not raced inside the walk. A hang there leaves the source's walk chain held after the record says `timed-out`, so the next rebuild on that node queues behind it and times out again (S2). A purge that answers late goes on to `completeBuild` (S1).
3. **pgvector.** The `pg_locks` query runs on `held.client`, the session that took the lock. The key is split into `classid`/`objid` with `objsubid = 1`, which is how a one-bigint advisory lock shows. A query error reads as lost, which fails safe. `completeBuild` checks the lock and `mine` before the switch transaction, and the generation check inside it. One race remains: the lock can be lost between `holdsBuilderLock` and the commit, and a builder that took up the source resumes the same generation id, so the own-generation check cannot tell the two apart (N2). The outcome is benign: same fingerprint, and the first build's walk was complete. A live lock is read as lost behind a transaction-mode pooler. That setup was already documented as unsupported, but before this change its builds ran with a warning. Now every complete build is refused at its first page (S3).
4. **Error codes.** Right. `LOCK_CONFLICT` 409 and `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` 409 match the catalog, both producers declare the status, and both baseline rows had to leave.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/service-knowledge` patch and `@objectstack/knowledge-pgvector` patch. Both packages publish what the diff changes. The PR body and the changeset body each carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. **Right.** Under AGENTS.md "Land it" item 3, a non-protocol widening ships at `patch`. No authorable key, value or metadata type changes, so `none` is right. Two values added to an exported output union is the widening arm the claim amend declared.
- Seat Q5, consumers of the two new states:
  - `os knowledge rebuild` (`packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/rebuild.ts`) continues only on `running`, succeeds only on `done`, and exits 1 with the record's message on anything else. Both new states are therefore read as failure, never as success.
  - `describeBuild` (`packages/cli/src/utils/knowledge-actions.ts`) prints the status verbatim. Its `running` checks are right for both.
  - The `rebuild` action's `running` guard (`knowledge-build-actions.ts`) lets a new rebuild start after either state.
  - `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` states both behaviours.
  - No `ui/` consumer exists.
  - The only miss is cosmetic: the CLI's mirror type `KnowledgeBuildView.status` and the two `not-run`/`failed` comments in `rebuild.ts` still list four states (N1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags and `open_questions`: the blocked report's two questions were both answered by the claim amend (Q1 option A, Q2 option A). The final report has `open_questions: []`. Its deviations: the `reindexWith` pass-through and import block are within the amend's intent, overlap-check was clean, and the `LOCK_CONFLICT` baseline row is right per ①. The trailer form is not this record's concern.
- N2 remainder: the stale building generation after a revert stays until the next build. It is named in the PR's acceptance notes and not filed. It needs no card now, because the rows are never read and the next build of any kind retires them. N4 is not implemented: the card marks it optional, and the fence removes its precondition.
- Seat Q6, the turso sibling: the note's premise is wrong. At this head, and on `main`, `knowledge-turso` throws `notReady(...)`, which is coded `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 ("The knowledge store (libSQL) is not ready: its source's index was switched while it searched"). The error is coded, but under the wrong code: the same condition is 409 `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` on pgvector and a 503 "store not ready" on turso, and the two carry different retry semantics. **Card-worthy**: a small p3 parity card for the zone. Fix: code it `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` 409 like pgvector. It is not a blocker here (N4).
- SQL push-down (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5): no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The lock check is one `EXISTS` over `pg_locks`. The own-generation check compares the at most two generation rows the existing locked read returns. Pass.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — `walkObjectSource` checks the fence once before the purge and never between the purge and `completeBuild`. A lease lost during a long purge is not seen. A purge hung past `BUILD_STALL_LIMIT_MS` that answers later goes on to complete the build after the lease was released, under a record that reads `timed-out`. Both contradict the new docs and jsdoc, which say neither stop purges or completes anything. pgvector's lock check still guards its switch, and the index stays correct, so this is a status and docs defect, not data loss. Fix: check `fence?.stop()` at the top of the private `completeBuild` helper, and add a test that loses the lease during the purge.
- S2 (should-fix) — `listAdapterDocuments`, `purgeDocuments` and `completeBuild` are not wrapped in `fencedCall`. A hang in any of them keeps the source's `reindexTails` chain held after `rebuildSource` has returned `timed-out`, so a new rebuild on that node waits behind the chain and times out again until a restart. That contradicts "a new rebuild can start without a restart" for "a store call that never answers". The hung-`completeBuild` test stops at the first record. Fix: race those three calls as the page-loop calls are, or narrow the docs to page calls.
- S3 (should-fix) — Behind a transaction-mode pooler, `holdsBuilderLock` reads a held lock as lost, so every complete pgvector build is now refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` at its first page. Before, it ran with a release warning. The `builderLost` remedy blames idle time or a dropped session. Fix: name the pooler cause in the remedy (as `releaseBuilderLock`'s warning does), and say in the changeset that such a deployment now fails its builds.
- N1 (nit) — `packages/cli/src/utils/knowledge-actions.ts` `KnowledgeBuildView.status` and the comments at `rebuild.ts` lines 23-24 and 67 still list four states. Runtime handling is right.
- N2 (nit) — pgvector `completeBuild`'s lock check runs before, and outside, the switch transaction. A lock lost in that window still switches, and a resumed builder shares the generation id, so the generation check cannot catch it. The outcome is benign; running the switch on the lock's own session would close the window.
- N3 (nit) — pgvector's `builds` entry outlives an abandoned build. Once that build's lock idles out, the first later `reason: 'reindex'` write, even a non-build `limit` reindex, is refused once with a "this build no longer holds the lock" message.
- N4 (nit) — The PR's acceptance note and the os-dev-report call turso's three-switch refusal "uncoded". It is `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503. Correct the note; the parity card in seat Q6 above carries the fix.
- N5 (nit) — knowledge-rag.mdx: "another node may build the source from then on" after `lease-lost`. On pgvector the stopped build's advisory lock stays on this node until `buildLockIdleMs`, so another node's build is refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` meanwhile. Item 5 already says so; a cross-reference would keep the two from reading as contradictory.

No must-fix: the card's acceptance holds. The per-page lease check has its lapsed-mid-walk test, the bound has its never-answering-embed test with the lease released and the next build `done`, pgvector's own-generation completion is coded and tested with two builders, and the docs state both stops. Every check-run is green.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37465-build-lease-fence`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5

1. **Shape**: draft against `main`. `service-knowledge`, `knowledge-pgvector`, docs, the error-status baseline. 9 files, +984/−37. Not governed, not security-touching. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at patch is right (record ②).
2. **Premise**: the lease fence, the 15-minute stall bound and the pgvector `pg_locks` check are sound, and the two 409 codes and the baseline removals are right.
3. **Gates**: contract record 7195078617 (`TIER_DEFAULT`) reads PASS, with three should-fix findings owed before landing. CI on this head: 0 failed. Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) skips on the PR, so the six live fence tests run only in the merge queue; the dev's local 83/83 stands until then.
4. **Owed before landing** (ids from the record):
   - **S1**: check `fence?.stop()` again in the private `completeBuild` helper, so a lease lost during the purge, or a purge that answers after the stall bound, completes nothing. Add a test that loses the lease during the purge.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fda121f9a6edf2713f0a03d3a622b0819ee6fd05`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta review. The previous record was at `50bac3562b1062b21d1054699579007a03ac54f8`. It covers the REWORK 7195089651, the os-dev-report 7196288912 and the claim amend 7196357662.

Inputs:
- the delta, `50bac3562..fda121f9a` (7 files, +149/−33)
- the net diff against `main` (11 files)
- the PR body as it now stands
- the changeset
- the check-runs on this head: 42 success, 17 skipped, 0 failure

Every required context is green: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate and Check Changeset. Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) is still skipped on the PR, so the live pgvector cases have only the dev's local reading (83/83) until the queue runs.

### ① Derived judgments

What the delta changes in the accept-set and the public surface:

- **The walk races the listing, `purgeDocuments` and `adapter.completeBuild` through `fencedCall`. The private `completeBuild` helper checks `fence.stop()` first.** No new export. Each refusal is an `ok: false` walk result, and the build record carries it as `timed-out` or `lease-lost`. Right as far as it goes; see S4, S5 and S6.
- **The pgvector `builderLost` remedy text names the transaction-mode pooler.** This changes operator text only; the code and status are unchanged. Right.
- **The CLI type `KnowledgeBuildView.status` gains the two states.** The type is internal: `packages/cli` exports `.`, `./console` and `./hook-body`, and none of them re-exports `utils/knowledge-actions.ts`. There is no runtime change. Right.

Prior ids:

- **S1 — closed.** The helper returns `ok: false` before `adapter.completeBuild` once the fence says stop. This covers a lease lost during the purge, and a purge that answers after the bound, now that the walk is no longer waiting on it. The new purge test pins the lease-lost case, and the dev reports its ablation red.
- **S2 — closed for the source's walk chain** (`reindexTails`). A hung listing, purge or `completeBuild` no longer holds it, and the hung-`completeBuild` case now reaches a second `done`. Two things are carried as new findings: what the purge race leaves on the per-document chain (S5), and what the `completeBuild` race opens (S4).
- **S3 — closed.** The `builderLost` remedy text and the changeset name the pooler and say such a deployment's builds are refused at the first page.
- **N1 — closed.**
- **N2 — stays open,** accepted by the seat (REWORK item 5).
- **N3 — stays open,** accepted by the seat (REWORK item 5).
- **N4 — closed.** The PR body now reads `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 and names parity card #37597, which is open.
- **N5 — closed.** The `lease-lost` bullet links item 5 and says another node's pgvector build is refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` until the idle time passes.

Judged as asked:

- **Can `fencedCall` around `completeBuild` abandon a switch that later commits after the record says `timed-out`? Yes, in two ways.**
  - **(a) No hang is needed.** pgvector's `completeBuild` commits the switch, then runs `sweepRetired`, which deletes the whole replaced generation in batches, inside the same call. That time counts against the stall bound, and the bound gets no tick after the last page (S6). So a large source whose fingerprint changed can commit its switch and then pass the bound in the sweep. The record then reads `timed-out` over a switched, current index.
  - **(b) A slow switch transaction** that commits after the bound does the same.
  - **What was already true at `50bac356`:** the record-level half, through `rebuildSource`'s race of the whole walk.
  - **What the delta adds:** it frees the source's chain while that `completeBuild` is still in flight. A rebuild on the same node — the obvious operator response to a `timed-out` record — now runs concurrently with it (S4).
- **Is the per-document `recordSyncTails` limit acceptable as named? Acceptable as a limit, not as named (S5).**
  - Keeping the per-document serialization is the safer side. If the chain were freed while the leaked delete is in flight, event sync for that document would race a late delete.
  - The note says the next build does not wait behind it. It does. The abandoned removal never landed, so the store still lists that document. The next complete build reads it as a purge candidate, serializes on the same held chain, and times out at its purge. The same happens on every build after it, until the call answers or the process restarts.
  - The new test hides this. Before the second build it swaps `listDocuments` for one that no longer lists the document, with the comment "the next build is run against a store that no longer lists it". A real store would still list it.
- **Is the `@objectstack/cli` changeset entry at the right level? Yes.**
  - `patch` is right: the CLI change is two comments and an internal, unexported type with no runtime change.
  - The changeset carries one `Clause-②` line for the whole file, and `yes (widening)` is owed by `@objectstack/service-knowledge`'s exported `KnowledgeBuildRecord.status`.
  - For the CLI alone the arm would be `no`. AGENTS.md "Land it" item 3 sets the level by kind, and a non-protocol change ships at patch either way. Adding a package under the file's existing declaration is right, and Check Changeset is green.
  - The added changeset sentence describes behaviour that was already true at runtime (`os knowledge rebuild` exits 1 on any status other than `done`), and it says so accurately.

### ② Semver level

Changeset:
- `@objectstack/service-knowledge`: patch
- `@objectstack/knowledge-pgvector`: patch
- `@objectstack/cli`: patch

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand in both the PR body and the changeset. They are right, unchanged from the prior record. The delta publishes no new export and no authorable key.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flags.**
  - The final report has `open_questions: []`.
  - Its deviations are all ordered by the rework and covered by claim amend 7196357662: the private `completeBuild` helper, the listing and purge call sites, and `packages/cli`.
  - Overlap with #37578 on `rebuild.ts` is reported clean.
  - The turso parity sibling is filed as #37597.
  - The per-document chain note is judged above (S5). One part of it is also wrong: it says "freeing it would mean changing `chainAfter` or `purgeDocuments`". The `serialize` lambda is built inside `walkObjectSource`, so the chain could be fenced there. Whether it should be is S5's trade-off.
- **SQL push-down** (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5): the delta adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Pass.

Findings:

- **S4 (should-fix) — a `completeBuild` the walk stopped waiting on clears a newer build's lock and fence on the same node.**
  - Once `fencedCall` abandons `adapter.completeBuild`, the source chain is free while that call still runs. A rebuild on the same node then calls `beginBuild`. `takeBuilderLock` adopts the very lock the in-flight call holds, because `holdsBuilderLock` reads it as held, and `builds` is set for the new build.
  - When the old call settles, its `finally` runs `builds.delete(sourceId)` and `releaseBuilderLock(sourceId)`. From then on the new build writes unfenced (`fenceBuild` returns early with no `builds` entry) and holds no advisory lock, so another node's build is admitted.
  - The new build's `completeBuild` is then refused `LOCK_CONFLICT`.
  - Both sweeps of the retired generation also run at once: the new `beginBuild` sweep and the old call's sweep. That is N4's leftover-rows case, which the PR says the fence now excludes.
  - The index stays correct: same fingerprint, and the docs already accept two builders. What breaks is the PR's own fence guarantee, and the records mislead (`timed-out` over a committed switch, then `failed`).
  - Fix, either of:
    - in pgvector, tie the `builds` entry and the lock release to the build that took them (a per-build token), and refuse to adopt a held lock while this adapter's own `completeBuild` is in flight;
    - in the service, keep `reindexTails` held until an abandoned `completeBuild` settles. This brings back a hang for that one call only, and should be named.
  - Either way, say in the docs and jsdoc that a completion the build stopped waiting on may still switch, so `timed-out` does not prove "nothing completed".
- **S5 (should-fix) — the named per-document limit understates its effect.**
